Calculate summaries across columns within each row

Source: R/row-stats.R
row_egen.Rd

  • row_mean(), row_sum(), and row_median() calculate row arithmetic.

  • row_min() and row_max() select the smallest and largest row values.

  • row_var() and row_sd() calculate sample variance and standard deviation.

  • row_unique() counts distinct values, including one missing category. row_nvals() follows egenmore's egen rownvals() and ignores missing values unless .missing = TRUE, when it equals row_unique().

  • row_miss() and row_non_miss() count missing and observed values.

Usage

row_mean(..., na.rm = TRUE)

row_sum(..., na.rm = TRUE)

row_max(..., .values = NULL, na.rm = TRUE)

row_min(..., .values = NULL, na.rm = TRUE)

row_median(..., na.rm = TRUE)

row_var(..., na.rm = TRUE)

row_sd(..., na.rm = TRUE)

row_unique(...)

row_nvals(..., .missing = FALSE)

row_miss(...)

row_non_miss(...)

Arguments

...

A data frame or tibble, or <tidy-select> expressions inside dplyr::mutate(). Each selected column must be one-dimensional.

na.rm

For arithmetic and extrema helpers, a single logical value. If TRUE (the default), omit missing values; if FALSE, any missing input makes that row's result missing. Count helpers (row_unique(), row_miss(), row_non_miss()) reject na.rm.

.values

For row_min() and row_max(), additional values to compare with selected columns: a vector, or a list of vectors. Each must have length one or the number of input rows (the current group size inside grouped mutate()). Values must have compatible supported types.

.missing

For row_nvals(), a single TRUE or FALSE. If FALSE (the default), missing values are not counted, as in egenmore's rownvals(); if TRUE, they count as one value, as in row_unique().

Value

A vector with one value per input row. Extrema retain the compatible common type; arithmetic returns doubles or a supported class as described above; unique and missing-value counts return integers.

Details

All helpers preserve the input. Missingness is determined from the original columns, including tagged and SPSS user-missing values. Arithmetic and extrema omit missing values by default. All-missing rows return a typed NA, except row_sum(na.rm = TRUE) returns zero. Variance and standard deviation use the sample denominator and require at least two observed values. Zero-row inputs return typed empty vectors; NULL and zero selected columns are rejected.

Extrema

row_min() and row_max() retain the compatible common type of the selected columns. Logical inputs return logical values, integer inputs return integers, and mixed logical/integer/double inputs use their common numeric type. Supported ordered types also include character vectors, ordered factors, Date, POSIXct, durations, measured vectors, integer64, and labelled vectors. Character values use C lexical ordering without numeric parsing; ordered factors use their level order and cannot be mixed with other types. Labelled values are compared by their underlying values. Compatible units are normalized before comparison. Unordered factors, lists, complex values, and incompatible combinations are rejected rather than assigned an arbitrary ordering. Like pmin() and pmax(), bare numeric constants in row_min() and row_max() are values, not column positions: row_min(x, 0.5) caps x at 0.5. Inside mutate(), a symbol that is not a column but names a numeric vector in the calling environment is also used as values. Select columns by position with c() or a tidyselect helper, for example row_min(c(1, 2)). Length-one constants (including those in .values) never fill a row whose other inputs are all missing; such rows stay NA, as with pmin().

Arithmetic

Plain logical, integer, double, and numeric labelled columns return double vectors. Labels are dropped after applying the original missingness mask. integer64 arithmetic requires explicit conversion so potential precision loss is a deliberate choice.

Columns from the same calendar family (Date or POSIXct) support mean and median while retaining their common class and metadata. Calendar sums, variance, and standard deviation require explicit numeric conversion first. Durations support mean, median, sum, and standard deviation and return difftime vectors in a common unit. For duration variance, explicitly convert to one numeric unit first because variance has squared units.

Compatible measured vectors on linear zero-origin scales are normalized to a common unit. Mean, median, sum, and standard deviation retain that unit; variance returns squared units. Offset scales such as Celsius and Fahrenheit support mean and median only. Convert explicitly to a zero-origin unit before requesting sums or dispersion. Nonlinear scales require explicit conversion to a linear unit before any arithmetic. Other classes and incompatible type combinations are rejected. Measured arithmetic requires units >= 1.0.0.

Counts

row_unique() combines compatible column types and counts distinct values without dropping their identities through numeric conversion. This includes compatible factors, labelled vectors, calendar/measured vectors, integer64, list columns, and complex vectors. Missing values count as one category. List elements are compared as whole values rather than flattened. For extrema and distinct counts, common-type conversion must preserve each original value's missingness. Conflicting SPSS missing-value definitions that would turn an observed value into a missing value produce an error; harmonize those definitions explicitly before combining the columns.

row_miss() and row_non_miss() use each original column's is.na() result. Scalar missing list elements are missing; NULL and empty list elements are observed. Count helpers return integer vectors.

Implementation

All row summaries and counts use native C++ kernels registered through cpp11, which read logical, integer and double columns directly and count missing values in the same pass. Means and sums give the same results as base::rowMeans() and base::rowSums() without first copying the columns into a matrix. Rfast is no longer required.

See also

Other variable generation functions: as_dummy(), cut, panel, std()

Examples

tb <- tibble::tibble(x = c(1, 2, NA), y = c(3, NA, NA))
row_mean(tb)
#> [1]  2  2 NA
row_sum(tb)
#> [1] 4 2 0
row_non_miss(tb)
#> [1] 2 1 0

tb |>
  dplyr::mutate(mean = row_mean(x, y), sum = row_sum(x, y))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>       x     y  mean   sum
#>   <dbl> <dbl> <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1     1     3     2     4
#> 2     2    NA     2     2
#> 3    NA    NA    NA     0
tb |>
  dplyr::mutate(capped = row_min(x, .values = 0.5))
#> # A tibble: 3 × 3
#>       x     y capped
#>   <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#> 1     1     3    0.5
#> 2     2    NA    0.5
#> 3    NA    NA   NA  
row_sum(tb, na.rm = FALSE)
#> [1]  4 NA NA

flags <- tibble::tibble(a = c(TRUE, FALSE, NA), b = c(FALSE, NA, NA))
row_max(flags) # TRUE, FALSE, NA, with logical type
#> [1]  TRUE FALSE    NA

dates <- tibble::tibble(
  start = as.Date(c("2024-01-01", NA)),
  end = as.Date(c("2024-01-03", "2024-01-05"))
)
row_min(dates)
#> [1] "2024-01-01" "2024-01-05"
row_mean(dates)
#> [1] "2024-01-02" "2024-01-05"
